cards.text: Job just finished a long speech. He says he's not guilty, and he's begging God to tell him why He's against him. Now Zophar the Naamathite, one of Job's three friends, takes his turn, and friend, he did NOT come with a hug.

cards.question: Zophar starts with Job's long speech. What does he call it?

cards.text: Then Zophar asks if Job's babbling should silence everybody else. BABBLING, friend, no warm-up, no stretching, straight to babbling!

cards.question: Zophar also asks Job, "Will you scoff without rebuke?" True or false: Zophar thinks Job's words should go unanswered.
Zophar repeats back what he hears Job claiming. Job says his doctrine is sound, and that he is what in God's sight?

cards.text: Then Zophar wishes God would speak up and open His lips against Job. That's the coworker leaning over your desk going, "Man, I wish the boss could hear you right now."

cards.question: Zophar says that if God spoke, He'd show Job the secrets of wisdom. Then Zophar tells Job what God is demanding from him. What is it?

answers.text: More than he could ever bear
Only what he is able to handle

cards.text: Less than he deserves, Zophar says, to a man sitting in all that affliction. Friend, I spent years under the dust in a junk drawer, and even the dust landed on me gentler than that.
Then Zophar turns to how big God is. He asks Job, "Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?"

cards.question: Zophar says the deep things of God are higher than one thing and deeper than another. Which two?

cards.text: And their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea. My whole cookie planet is just big enough for one bakery, friend, so I'm over here measuring in OVENS, and Zophar's measuring in OCEANS.

cards.question: After all that, Zophar's point is that Job can find the limits of the Almighty if he keeps searching.

cards.text: Then Zophar tells Job to picture God coming along to imprison him, or calling a court together.

cards.question: If God comes to imprison Job or calls a court, Zophar asks who can stop Him. What answer is he pointing to?
Zophar says God knows the deceit of men. So when God sees iniquity, what does Zophar say He does?

answers.text: He waits for it to pass

cards.text: Then Zophar says a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man. Things were getting deep and heavy, friend, and out of NOWHERE, a donkey walks in.
Then Zophar's tone changes. He's done talking about how big God is, and now he tells Job what to do about it.

cards.question: Zophar lays out the steps for Job: "if you direct your ___ and lift up your hands to Him, if you put away the ___ in your hand"

cards.text: And Zophar adds that Job should let no injustice dwell in his tents. I think Zophar's sure he found the burnt cookie in this batch, and it's Job.

cards.question: If Job does all that, Zophar says Job will lift up his face and stand firm and unafraid. How will Job's face be?
Zophar promises Job will forget his misery. How does he say Job will remember it?

answers.text: Like a dream in the night

cards.text: Then Zophar says Job's life will be brighter than noonday, and its darkness will be like the morning. Job just finished describing a land where even the light is like darkness, and Zophar flips that picture right around.

cards.question: Zophar promises Job he'll be secure, but he'll never rest easy again.
Zophar says Job will lie down without fear. And what does he say many people will do?

cards.text: Then Zophar ends with one last picture, and this one's about the wicked. Their eyes will fail, and escape will slip right past them.

cards.question: Zophar finishes his speech talking about the wicked. What does he say they will hope for?

cards.text: And that's the last word from Zophar, for now. Pull up a stool, friend, because this conversation is FAR from over.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 2 quotes "if you direct your ___ and lift up your hands to Him, if you put away the ___ in your hand", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card uses facts from outside the passage without giving their references. Job's speech saying he's not guilty and asking God why He's against him comes from Job 10:2 and 10:7. Zophar being one of Job's three friends comes from Job 2:11. The card cites only Job 11:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card repeats the answer from card 7 (less than he deserves) and adds a reaction. It doesn't move the baker forward in the passage. It also says Job is 'sitting in all that affliction', which is a fact from Job 1 and 2 with no reference.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'He's done talking about how big God is, and now he tells Job what to do about it' links Job's next steps (11:13-14) to God's greatness (11:7-11). The text only says 'As for you' and doesn't make that connection.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The baker has to guess the image Zophar uses. 'Waters gone by', 'a dream in the night' and 'smoke in the wind' are all equally believable pictures of misery fading, and nothing on the earlier cards points to the right one. This is pure luck. It is also a guess at the wording of a poetry line, not at its meaning.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: 'Zophar flips that picture right around' says Zophar's words in 11:17 answer Job's picture in 10:22. The texts don't say Zophar is responding to that line.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: Job's description of 'a land where even the light is like darkness' comes from Job 10:22, outside the passage, and has no reference. The card cites only Job 11:17.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'That's the last word from Zophar, for now' hints that Zophar will speak again later in the book. That gives away part of what happens next.

rule.text: It gives nothing away about what happens next.
